study_guide.title: Watch and Warning

pages.text: Cane the Weather Dog was watching the weather report with his family. He heard the reporter use two important words: watch… and warning. "Those two words sound alike," said Cane, "but they mean different things. Let's learn them, because knowing the difference helps keep us safe." First, a watch. "A watch means a storm is possible," said Cane. "It's a heads-up. When there's a watch, we watch the sky and start getting ready — calm and early." Then, a warning. "A warning is stronger," said Cane. "A warning means a storm is expected — it's really coming. When there's a warning, we take action now and do our family plan." "Here's an easy way to remember it," Cane said with a smile. "Think about dinner. When a grown-up says, 'We might eat soon — go wash your hands,' that's like a watch. Get ready! But when they say, 'Dinner is ready NOW — come sit down,' that's like a warning. Do it right away!" Cane practiced the rule until he knew it by heart: Watch = get ready. Warning = act now.
pages.ask: Can you say it? A watch means… get ready! And a warning means… act now! Which one means 'right now' — a watch or a warning? (A warning!)

pages.text: A few days later, the weather people said a hurricane was far out at sea. First came a watch. Cane's family stayed calm and checked their prep kit and their plan.
Then the watch became a warning. "The storm is expected now," said Cane. "Time to do our plan." His family didn't panic — they just followed the steps they had practiced, and everyone was safe.
"See?" said Cane. "When you know what the words mean, big storms aren't so scary. You just listen, and you know exactly what to do. Great job, weather watcher!"

study_guide.rule: Watch = get ready. Warning = act now!

cards.def: what we do and where we go to be safe
a storm is expected — act now
a storm is possible — get ready

choices: a storm is possible — get ready
there is no storm at all
it is time for a nap
a storm is expected and coming — act now
